title: Factors Associated with Perceived Anticipatory Organizational Socialization Among Nursing Students: Self-Leadership, Person-Centered Care, and Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence
content: Background/Objectives: Perceived anticipatory organizational socialization may help nursing students prepare for the transition to professional practice. Guided by the newcomer adjustment model, this study examined the associations of self-leadership, person-centered care, and attitudes toward artificial intelligence (AI) with organizational socialization among nursing students. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 142 third- and fourth-year nursing students from two programs in the Republic of Korea completed an online questionnaire; after the exclusion of 11 respondents with missing or invalid covariate responses, 131 were analyzed. Data were analyzed using Pearson correlations and hierarchical multiple linear regression. Results: Organizational socialization was correlated with self-leadership (r = 0.62, p < 0.001) and person-centered care (r = 0.34, p < 0.001), but not with attitudes toward AI (r = 0.13, p = 0.148). After adjustment for year of study and major satisfaction, only self-leadership was independently associated with organizational socialization (β = 0.505, p < 0.001); the final model explained 43.9% of the variance. Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent findings for self-leadership. Conclusions: Self-leadership was the characteristic most closely associated with nursing students' perceived preparedness for organizational adaptation, whereas general attitudes toward AI were not. Self-leadership development is a candidate target for educational interventions; longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to determine whether it supports actual adaptation after employment.
